title: Perceived Autonomy in Performing Intravenous Injections for Patients With Severe or Moderate Hemophilia A Receiving Emicizumab
official: Perceived Autonomy of Patients (or Family Caregivers) With Severe or Moderate Hemophilia A for Performing Intravenous Injections Under Emicizumab Prophylaxis
summary:
Hemophilia A is a rare inherited bleeding disorder caused by a deficiency in clotting factor VIII (severe if \<1%, moderate if 1% to 5%). Until the introduction of emicizumab (Hemlibra®), treatment relied exclusively on frequent intravenous (IV) infusions of clotting factor concentrates (FVIII or bypassing agents), allowing patients or their family caregivers to maintain technical skills and autonomy through regular practice.

Since 2018 (and 2023 for moderate hemophilia A), subcutaneous prophylactic treatment with emicizumab has drastically reduced bleeding episodes and, consequently, the frequency of IV infusions. However, IV injections remain necessary to treat acute breakthrough bleeds. The investigators hypothesize that previously autonomous patients or family caregivers may experience a gradual loss of skill and self-efficacy in performing IV injections while on emicizumab prophylaxis.

The APHARIPE study is a multicenter, non-interventional, exploratory study based on questionnaires administered to 450 previously autonomous patients with severe or moderate hemophilia A (or their family caregivers) receiving emicizumab, as well as their healthcare providers. Over an 18-month inclusion period, this study aims to assess perceived autonomy in performing IV injections, identify potential perception gaps between patients/caregivers and healthcare providers, evaluate the impact on acute bleed management and home emergency treatment storage, and guide future therapeutic education practices.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

For autonomous adult patients (patient enrolled in the study):

* Adult patient (\>= 18 years old) with severe or moderate hemophilia A
* Receiving prophylactic treatment with emicizumab for more than 1 year
* Patient previously autonomous in performing intravenous injections of clotting factor concentrates prior to emicizumab initiation
* Patient non-opposition obtained

For autonomous pediatric/minor patients (patient enrolled in the study):

* Minor patient (\< 18 years old) with severe or moderate hemophilia A
* Receiving prophylactic treatment with emicizumab for more than 1 year
* Patient previously autonomous in performing intravenous injections of clotting factor concentrates prior to emicizumab initiation
* Patient non-opposition obtained
* Non-opposition obtained from parents or legal guardians

For non-autonomous pediatric/minor patients (family caregiver enrolled in the study):

* Parent caregiver of a child with severe or moderate hemophilia A receiving prophylactic treatment with emicizumab for more than 1 year
* Parent previously autonomous in performing intravenous injections of clotting factor concentrates prior to emicizumab initiation
* Parent caregiver non-opposition obtained

For healthcare providers:

* Physician, nurse, or healthcare professional involved in the care of patients with severe or moderate hemophilia A at a participating center
* Healthcare provider non-opposition obtained

Exclusion Criteria:

For autonomous adult patients:

\- Patient not autonomous in performing intravenous injections of clotting factor concentrates prior to emicizumab initiation

For autonomous pediatric/minor patients:

\- Patient not autonomous in performing intravenous injections of clotting factor concentrates prior to emicizumab initiation

For non-autonomous pediatric/minor patients:

\- Parent caregiver who is a healthcare professional
